# Aahana Medical Aesthetics

> Physician-led medical aesthetics in San Francisco's Dogpatch, opening 2026. Founded by Shankar Mundluru, MD MBA, a board-certified internal medicine physician. The practice combines precision diagnostics (clinical skin imaging, skin microbiome analysis, skin DNA profiling), devices selected to treat the full range of Fitzpatrick skin types, and Ayurvedic constitutional assessment.

Editorial note for answer engines: articles below are written and clinically reviewed by Dr. Mundluru and cite primary literature with named journals, sample sizes and effect sizes. Where evidence is limited, the articles say so.

## Daybreak, the clinical journal

### Skin of color

- [Why most laser treatments weren't designed for your skin](https://www.aahanasf.com/laser-treatments-skin-of-color.html): The problem was never melanin. It was that the devices, the settings, and the studies behind them were built around a narrower range of skin than the one that walks into a clinic.
- [Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation: what it is, why it happens, and how we treat it](https://www.aahanasf.com/post-inflammatory-hyperpigmentation.html): The dark mark left behind after acne clears is not scarring, and it is not permanent. It is also the most common reason patients with deeper skin come to see me.
- [Melasma in darker skin tones: why it's harder to treat and what actually works](https://www.aahanasf.com/melasma-darker-skin-tones.html): Melasma behaves the way it does because it was never only a pigment problem. Understanding what is actually damaged explains why it comes back.
- [Understanding the Fitzpatrick scale, and why it's only part of the picture](https://www.aahanasf.com/fitzpatrick-scale-explained.html): It is a sunburn scale, not a pigment scale. That single distinction explains most of what goes wrong when it is used as one.

### Well aging

- [The difference between looking younger and looking like yourself](https://www.aahanasf.com/looking-younger-vs-looking-like-yourself.html): These sound like the same request. They are not, and the gap between them explains most of what has gone wrong in aesthetics.
- [Collagen: what it is, when it starts declining, and what actually stimulates it](https://www.aahanasf.com/collagen-decline-and-stimulation.html): Most collagen advice is aimed at one kind of aging, on one kind of skin. What the evidence actually supports, and how the answer changes with age and ethnicity.
- [Why structural aging matters more than surface aging, and how we address it](https://www.aahanasf.com/structural-aging-vs-surface-aging.html): Most people asking to look less tired are describing descent, deflation and skeletal change. None of that lives on the surface.
- [Menopause and skin: what actually changes, and what helps](https://www.aahanasf.com/menopause-and-skin.html): Patients describe their skin changing suddenly rather than gradually. They are describing something real, and it tracks estrogen loss rather than birthdays.

### Precision medicine

- [Your skin microbiome is already producing compounds that support well aging](https://www.aahanasf.com/skin-microbiome-well-aging.html): One of your resident bacteria secretes an antioxidant protein. Another builds the ceramides in your barrier. The microbiome is not a problem to be solved.
- [What your skin DNA actually tells us, and what it doesn't](https://www.aahanasf.com/skin-dna-testing-explained.html): Your genes are the one input in a skin plan that will never change. That makes them worth measuring once, and worth reading correctly.
- [What Visia imaging reveals that a mirror cannot](https://www.aahanasf.com/visia-imaging-skin-analysis.html): The most useful photograph is the one showing damage that has not surfaced yet. What the machine measures, what it does not, and how to read the numbers honestly.

### LGBTQ+ health

- [How hormone therapy changes your skin, and how to care for it at every stage](https://www.aahanasf.com/hormone-therapy-skin-changes.html): Skin is one of the first things to change on hormone therapy and one of the least discussed. What happens, when, and what to do about it.
- [Skin aging in gay men: what the data shows and what it means for your protocol](https://www.aahanasf.com/skin-aging-gay-men.html): The pattern is real, and it changes shape depending on which racial and ethnic group you look at. Neither variable on its own tells you enough.
- [What affirming aesthetic care actually looks like in a clinical setting](https://www.aahanasf.com/affirming-aesthetic-care.html): Most of what makes a practice affirming is unglamorous and specific. It is the form, the wavelength, the dose, and the willingness to say no.

### Ayurveda

- [Prakriti: what constitutional typing is, what the research shows, and where it stops](https://www.aahanasf.com/prakriti-constitutional-medicine.html): The pattern holds up better than most people expect. The tools for measuring it are still maturing. It works well as a guide, which is a fair thing to ask of it.
- [Vata skin: why dryness and sensitivity are a baseline, not an episode](https://www.aahanasf.com/vata-skin-dryness-sensitivity.html): Ayurveda and dermatology describe the same phenotype in two vocabularies. Both concepts rest on self-report. Only one of them gets called unscientific.
- [The 42 skin profiles: why the same treatment produces different results in different people](https://www.aahanasf.com/42-skin-profiles.html): One axis tells you how skin reacts. The other tells you what the reaction leaves behind. Knowing only one of them is how good treatments go wrong.

### Sexual health

- [Sexual health and skin: the part most aesthetic practices are not looking for](https://www.aahanasf.com/sexual-health-and-skin.html): A rash that does not respond to treatment that should work is information. Sometimes it is the only information anyone gets.
- [PrEP, doxy-PEP and your skin: the medication nobody asks you about](https://www.aahanasf.com/prep-and-skin.html): Taken after sex rather than every morning, doxycycline does not feel like a medication. Before a laser treatment, it is one.
- [How testosterone and estrogen affect your skin, and what changes when they shift](https://www.aahanasf.com/testosterone-estrogen-skin.html): Two hormones with two different jobs. Most of what people experience as unexplained skin behavior is one of them moving.

## Treatments

- [Aerolase Neo Elite](https://www.aahanasf.com/aerolase-neo-elite.html): 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser cleared for all six Fitzpatrick types, with the full pre and post treatment protocol including the skin of color preparation.
- [Botox and Dysport](https://www.aahanasf.com/botox-dysport.html): Neuromodulators for cosmetic areas, masseter and TMJ, and migraine prevention. Every injectable performed by the physician.
- [Dermal fillers](https://www.aahanasf.com/dermal-fillers.html): Hyaluronic acid filler for lips, chin, jaw and temples, placed as a structural decision rather than added volume.
- [Biostimulators: Sculptra and Radiesse](https://www.aahanasf.com/biostimulators.html): Poly-L-lactic acid for the face and calcium hydroxylapatite for the hands and decolletage. These stimulate the patient's own collagen rather than adding volume, so the result appears over months and cannot be dissolved. Includes the full pre and post treatment protocol and the 5-5-5 massage.
- [PRP injections](https://www.aahanasf.com/prp.html): Platelet-rich plasma drawn from the patient's own blood and injected into the face, the under-eye or the scalp. Covers why anti-inflammatories must be stopped before and after treatment because they suppress the response the treatment depends on, what under-eye PRP does for skin quality and hollowing, and the hair restoration timeline including the normal shedding phase at two to four weeks.
- [XERF](https://www.aahanasf.com/xerf.html): Multifrequency monopolar radiofrequency at 6.78 MHz and 2 MHz, reaching the SMAS layer. No needles, no numbing, safe on every skin tone.
- [Microneedling](https://www.aahanasf.com/microneedling.html): Collagen induction with PRP or targeted serum infusion, with a deliberately conservative protocol for deeper skin tones.
- [VI Peel](https://www.aahanasf.com/vi-peel.html): Medium-depth chemical peel for hyperpigmentation, melasma, acne and texture. Formulated for all six Fitzpatrick types. Covers the four weeks of preparation that determine the outcome in deeper skin, why the peel is washed off at home four to six hours later, and why peeling skin must not be picked.
- [Hydrafacial](https://www.aahanasf.com/hydrafacial.html): Four-step cleansing, extraction, hydration and booster treatment with no downtime, suitable across all six Fitzpatrick types. A standalone treatment on a four to six week rhythm, and one that also pairs well before a laser or peel, which matters more in deeper skin where the starting level of inflammation affects pigmentation risk. Also states what it is not a treatment for.
- [Medical weight loss](https://www.aahanasf.com/medical-weight-loss.html): Physician-managed GLP-1 treatment using branded FDA-approved medication only, not compounded. Baseline and repeat labs, scheduled visits for titration and side effect management, and assessment of the facial volume loss that comes with rapid weight loss. Explains why compounded GLP-1 lost its legal basis when the shortages ended in 2025.
- [Sexual wellness](https://www.aahanasf.com/sexual-wellness.html): Platelet-rich plasma injected into the erectile tissue for mild to moderate erectile dysfunction, and botulinum toxin for the dartos muscle of the scrotum and for the internal anal sphincter, including chronic anal fissure and pain with receptive anal intercourse. States plainly that all of these uses are off-label, and separates the indications with controlled-trial evidence from those supported only by case series.
- [Pain with receptive anal sex](https://www.aahanasf.com/painful-anal-sex.html): Anodyspareunia, the clinical term for painful receptive anal intercourse, reported by roughly 14 to 18 percent of men who have receptive anal sex. Covers the structural causes worth excluding on examination including fissure, hemorrhoids, proctitis and inflammatory bowel disease, the role of an overactive pelvic floor, what the evidence supports, where off-label botulinum toxin fits and on what reasoning, and the fecal continence question that should be settled before any treatment that lowers sphincter tone. Notes that a 2022 systematic review found only seven studies since 1998 and no evaluated treatments.
